text: Working with APIs is a common task for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. To access protected resources, you often need authentication, such as an API key or a token. Be careful with rate limits, because sending too many requests can get you blocked. Finally, always add error handling to your code, so your application can respond gracefully when something goes wrong.
